scenes.line1: Why do E2E tests fail randomly?
scenes.say: Why do end-to-end tests sometimes fail for no clear reason? What actually causes flakiness?

scenes.label: E2E
scenes.sub: Simulates real user flows across your whole system.
scenes.say: End-to-end tests simulate real user flows across your entire system. They're great for catching issues that unit tests miss.
But E2E tests are prone to flakiness. Timing issues, network delays, or unstable external APIs can cause random failures. This undermines trust in your test suite.

scenes.title: Cypress Test Output
scenes.say: Here's a real example. A Cypress end-to-end test fails sometimes when the API is slow. The test passes or fails at random.
To reduce flakiness, I control test data, use retries only when needed, and keep E2E tests focused on the most critical flows.

scenes.question: Should you add retries to every E2E test?
scenes.right: No. Use retries sparingly or you might hide real bugs.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Should you add retries to every end-to-end test? No. Use retries only when necessary, or you might end up hiding real bugs.
